name: Preflop Blueprint
subject: An open dark drafting folio containing a large tactile six-max opening-range plan: six distinct seat sectors, stepped clusters of cobalt and silver square tiles, and a chrome drafting compass resting across one corner. The tiles are blank, showing varying range breadth without pretending to be a readable chart.
camera: True overhead, flat and architectural, with the folio tilted slightly within the landscape frame.
composition: The open folio fills nearly the entire image. Broad blocks of tiles occupy the left two-thirds; six seat sectors fan across the right. Use matte blueprint paper, satin metal, crisp shadows and a restrained blue edge light. No round stage, pedestal, distant room, card space or chip towers.
reuseReview: Viewed at 640px. Six chip stacks sit symmetrically on the same circular chrome stage around a large empty card area; no range blueprint is visible.

name: C-Bet Academy
subject: A close poker-table decision scene in which a modest continuation bet has just slid away from a larger existing pot. Two unlettered chrome sizing dividers compare the bet footprint with the pot footprint, making the sizing relationship the subject.
camera: Low oblique viewpoint from the flop side of a real black felt table, shallow enough to see chip heights.
composition: A natural patch of felt at lower left accommodates a real three-card flop overlay. The pot sits high at center; the smaller bet runs diagonally toward lower right. The two sizing dividers cut across the diagonal rather than forming a platform. The felt, real table rail and asymmetric chip movement fill the scene.
reuseReview: Viewed at 640px. Three ascending stacks and calipers occupy the right side of the repeated circular platform; the entire left side is reserved for cards.

name: Defense Matrix
subject: An incoming stream of cobalt chips reaches a defensive decision wall made of three broad hinged chrome shutters. One shutter absorbs the pressure, one opens a narrow continuation route, and one redirects the flow. It is a visual metaphor for choosing a response to aggression, not a cage around a chip stack.
camera: Three-quarter cutaway from below the left edge, looking through the staggered shutters.
composition: A strong zigzag fills the full width: incoming chips at upper left, three overlapping shutters through the center, and a single open lane exiting at lower right. Use large dark negative shapes between shutters, with precise bright edges. No circular object, chip tower, pedestal or card overlay.
reuseReview: Viewed at 640px. A caged chip stack sits at left on the repeated mirrored circle with vacant right half; the metaphor is generic and no aggression decision is legible.

name: Value Extractor
subject: An extreme close-up of one extra matching cobalt chip being slid into the edge of a modest pot by a black-sleeved human hand. That small final chip, almost touching the larger collection, communicates extracting one more call.
camera: Macro at felt level, with the focal plane on the narrow gap between the moving chip and the pot.
composition: The fingertips enter from the upper-right crop; the existing pot is cropped large on the lower-left. The final chip lies between them with its polished silver edge catching a narrow light. Most of the frame is tactile felt and the edges of real poker chips. No machine, plate, circular stage or generic stack display.
reuseReview: Viewed at 640px. A mechanical grabber and chip stack repeat the right-side product pose and circular stage; thin value is not clearly distinguished.

name: Bluff Catcher
subject: A tense cinematic hero-call moment: a calm adult poker player's eyes watch an oversized opposing wager across the felt while their fingers hold one calling chip at the edge of the betting line. Render the face in cool silver monochrome and the clothing in black.
camera: Eye-level telephoto crop across the table; the eyes occupy the upper band and the poised call occupies the lower foreground.
composition: The diagonal opposing wager creates the center-left foreground; the focused eyes span the upper right. The poised calling hand and chip remain fully visible at lower right without an overlay. Use a narrow cobalt reflection in the rail, not a luminous pedestal. Keep the expression readable rather than distant.
reuseReview: Viewed at 640px. A magnifying glass and stacks repeat the left-side product pose and mirrored circular stage; vacant right half dominates.
overlayReview: Native cards omitted after direct scene review so the hero-call gesture remains visible.

name: Position Power
subject: A real poker table seen down its long rail, contrasting an early-position seat half-hidden behind the curve with a clearly lit button seat that can see the whole action. A plain chrome dealer disc rests beside the far active seat.
camera: Long, compressed rail-level perspective with a strong near-to-far vanishing line.
composition: The curved stitched black rail sweeps from the lower-left foreground toward the far-right button. Two large seat backs, one near and partly occluding the action and one far and exposed, create the positional contrast. Small bet trails lie on the felt. No miniature table on a display platform and no card reserve area.
reuseReview: Viewed at 640px. A miniature table changes the subject but remains isolated at right on the same large circular studio platform; position advantage is weak.

name: 3-Bet Pots
subject: A substantial contested pot tightly squeezed between two shorter remaining chip reserves. Three broad action tracks feed the pot, but the available space behind each player's wager is visibly reduced, suggesting the lower room for maneuver after a preflop three-bet.
camera: Steep overhead trapezoidal crop of the actual felt, close enough to see individual chip edges.
composition: The large irregular pot dominates the middle diagonal. Two compact reserve clusters sit in opposite corners; broad chrome-inlaid bet tracks converge around them. The composition is compressed and crowded by design. No rings, arches, arena stage, decorative tower or card placeholders.
reuseReview: Viewed at 640px. Three arch rings frame an empty center with identical flank stacks; the elevated-pot concept is absent.

name: 4-Bet Wars
subject: Two opposing lines of escalating poker wagers rush toward one another: four chunky successive tiers of chips on each side, frozen at the moment the largest wagers meet. The scene should feel like a costly preflop confrontation, not a trophy.
camera: Dynamic diagonal viewpoint tilted above the felt, close enough for the nearest wager to feel oversized.
composition: Two opposing triangular masses occupy opposite corners and collide across the center. The fourth wager is largest and sharp; earlier tiers recede in softer focus. Restrained motion traces follow actual chip movement. Fill the frame with the confrontation, without a circular base or empty half.
reuseReview: Viewed at 640px. Four chip pillars on a circular platform repeat the same right-side composition; the sense of opposing preflop escalation is absent.

name: Deep Stack Cash
subject: A deep-stacked cash player's workspace viewed from high over the player's right shoulder. Two clear rectangular chip racks hold substantial, irregular reserves; a black-sleeved hand peels a small wager from the nearest column while several widely separated future wager piles remain available farther across the felt. The abundant reserve and room for later decisions communicate 200BB-plus play.
camera: Steep sixty-degree downward player-side close-up, explicitly showing the tops of every chip column. The player's cropped shoulder sits at the near-right edge. No low angle, corridor, horizon or view between chip towers.
composition: Two transparent rectangular reserve racks cross the lower-left diagonal; the hand reaches through the middle; several smaller prospective wagers spread toward the upper-right on real felt. Individual chip tops and the rack walls remain visible, so depth comes from a rich reserve workspace rather than a canyon. No mirrored display base, flanking walls of stacks, circular platform or empty card zone.
reuseReview: Viewed at 640px. Two towers on the left repeat the circular platform and huge empty right area; stack depth is represented but the layout is repetitive.
revisionReason: Resolve cross-category composition collision identified by root while preserving game-specific focus.

name: Short Stack Rat
subject: A sleek little gunmetal rat character rapidly slipping along a poker-table rail with a compact bundle of cobalt chips, while enormous out-of-focus opponent reserves loom behind. The compact take and quick exit express a short-stack hit-and-run strategy.
camera: Low tracking profile, near the rail and slightly ahead of the moving character.
composition: The rat stretches horizontally across the lower-middle frame, with its tail and the curved rail making a long sweep. A small opening in a chip rack at far right gives it a clear destination. Use a polished illustrated character style, black fur-like metal, silver whiskers and cobalt chips; no round podium or cards.

name: Donk Defense
subject: An unexpected lead bet arrives from the near blind seat before the far aggressor can act. The leading chips cross the usual flow of action at a sharp angle, while a defender's larger reserve and real hole cards wait beyond the crossing.
camera: Tight three-quarter view from just behind the leading seat, emphasizing the surprising diagonal entry.
composition: The lead bet enters large from the lower-left and cuts across the frame; the far player's chip reserve is at upper right. The actual A-heart and Q-spade cards sit in a modest natural patch of felt to the right. Include one chrome table-rail corner for orientation. No shields, cages or product stage.

name: River Decisions
subject: The final-street decision on a poker table: a completed five-card board divides a large opposing river bet from a small call chip poised at the near rail. The human hand has paused, conveying a consequential final choice.
camera: Directly overhead, tightly cropped to the river board and both sides of the decision.
composition: The actual five-card board forms a narrow horizontal band through the center. An irregular opposing wager fills the upper-left quadrant; the near hand and single call chip enter from lower right. The table edge curves along the bottom, closing the scene. No drawn cards or empty product-display area.

name: Probe Betting
subject: A neglected pot beyond an opponent's withdrawn hand, with a new line of cobalt betting chips confidently entering the open space. The withdrawal and the entering bet tell the checked-through-then-probe story without a literal scientific probe.
camera: Medium close table-height view from behind the player taking the initiative, with a strong depth change from hand to pot.
composition: A black sleeve and a low moving bet occupy the left foreground; the unused pot is clear at mid-right. The opponent's retreating hand recedes toward the upper crop. A thin horizontal silver rail binds the scene. Light reveals open felt ahead of the bet, not a reserved card slot.

name: Check-Raise Art
subject: A restrained first bet path makes a sharp return and rises into a much larger counter-wager. The visual is a sculptural poker-action U-turn: a small line of chips passes a recessed quiet zone and is met by a forceful returning wave.
camera: High three-quarter view of a broad S-shaped action path across felt.
composition: The small incoming line runs left to right along the upper third; a sweeping chrome turn carries the much larger cobalt counter-wager back across the lower third. The two movements occupy distinct planes and nearly cross. Use a bold graphic silhouette and no generic ramp on a pedestal.

name: Overbetting
subject: A wager dramatically larger than the existing pot, shown through extreme scale contrast. A dense rectangular wall of cobalt chips advances toward a small loose cluster of black-and-silver pot chips.
camera: Almost vertical aerial crop, offset toward the oversized wager.
composition: The large bet occupies the right two-thirds as an imposing rectangular mass; the small pot is isolated in the upper-left, with a narrow strip of felt between. One sharp shadow stretches from the bet toward the pot. Do not place the small pot in a bowl or put either group on a stage.

name: Multi-way Pots
subject: Four players' distinct betting motions meet in one contested poker pot. Black sleeves and cool monochrome hands approach from four edges; each player contributes a different-sized chip group.
camera: Bird's-eye close crop directly over the pot and hands.
composition: The irregular shared pot sits off center, and four incoming bets form unequal spokes. Hands and cuffs occupy the four corners, creating a lively interlocking shape rather than a symmetric diagram. Keep the hands large and the chip groups legible on mobile. No player portraits, rings, pedestal or decorative cards.

name: Rake Awareness
subject: A poker-table rake slot siphons one small chip away from a larger pot. A clear cutaway reveals that chip dropping into a separate collection tray beneath the felt, making the otherwise easy-to-ignore cost physically visible.
camera: Macro cross-section at the actual table edge, half above the felt and half below.
composition: The top-left shows the pot close to a narrow chrome slot; a single chip descends through the center; the bottom-right reveals the collection channel. Use a strong horizontal felt boundary, dark transparent cutaway glass and precise silver reflections. No scale, podium or playing cards.

name: Blind vs Blind
subject: Two adjacent blind seats clash across the tight elbow of a poker table. Their nearby chip reserves and opposing small wagers occupy the same corner while the rest of the table falls out of focus.
camera: Close high-angle view of one curved table corner, with the two neighboring seat backs partly visible.
composition: The table's chrome-edged elbow is the main shape, separating the seats along the lower-left and lower-right edges. The competing wagers face each other across a short diagonal on the felt. Make their adjacency clear; no generic distant heads-up table or duel shields.

name: Straddle Games
subject: A row of three forced bets expands along the opening edge of a cash table, with the added third straddle conspicuously larger and farther forward. A plain chrome marker beside the third post emphasizes the additional pressure.
camera: Very low lateral close-up, looking along the three distinct posts so their height and forward distance are visible.
composition: Small blind and big blind are partly cropped at the left; the larger straddle dominates the near-right foreground. The felt's stitched boundary runs diagonally behind them and bends outward around the third post. No orbit rings, numbered chips, floating platforms or card overlays.

name: Table Selection
subject: A compact overhead casino-floor study of three large cash-table sections: one crowded with imposing reserves, one nearly empty, and one with a clear inviting seat beside modest uneven stacks. A focused cobalt light picks out the strategically attractive seat.
camera: High bird's-eye architectural view, with three partial tables large enough to read as distinct situations.
composition: The three cropped table shapes make an offset mosaic rather than a row of miniature objects. The promising seat lies near the lower-middle and connects visually to an open aisle. Black upholstery and silver table edging establish the brand. No podiums, trophy, magnifying glass or cards.

name: Mixed Strategies
subject: A physical randomizer sorts identical poker chips into two action channels in an uneven but controlled mixture. Broad chrome baffles and dark branching paths make the distribution visible without numbers or a fabricated chart.
camera: Straight-on cutaway of a tall rectangular mechanism, tilted a few degrees for depth.
composition: A single narrow feed enters from upper left, crosses a staggered field of large baffles, then splits into two broad lower trays of different fullness. The device fills the frame edge to edge. Use a layered editorial illustration with matte ink navy and satin chrome, not a polished circular product stage.

name: Texture Reading
subject: A tactile split poker-analysis surface: one side smooth, dry and sparsely patterned, the other interconnected by dense cobalt channels. The contrasting surfaces express how connectedness changes board texture. There are absolutely no playing cards or card-shaped objects in this generated scene.
camera: Frontal tabletop close-up with a shallow downward angle, keeping the board large and readable.
composition: The smooth black plane on the left transitions into a connected blue-and-chrome relief on the right, filling the lower half. Keep a natural uninterrupted dark-felt band through the upper-middle area for three actual Club Arena cards to be added later by the application; those cards are NOT part of this image. Do not draw white rectangles, blank cards, card outlines, letters or rank symbols. No chip stacks.

name: Equity Denial
subject: A firm betting barrier closes the routes that drawing hands could otherwise take to a protected pot. Thin cobalt paths approach from the left and terminate at a broad angular chrome shutter driven into place by a compact wager.
camera: Side-on horizontal cutaway, close to the moving shutter and the interrupted paths.
composition: The betting shutter slices diagonally down through the middle. Several delicate incoming paths occupy the left third; the protected pot is partly visible behind the shutter at far right. The shutter and the cut-off glow carry the image, not a chip tower. No round stage, shields or cards.

name: Pot Control
subject: A calm human hand holds back further chips at the rim of a modest existing pot. A low transparent acrylic stop, lit silver-blue, makes the intentional limit visible without portraying the hand as weak or passive.
camera: Intimate over-the-shoulder crop, focused on the flat restraining hand and the manageable pot size.
composition: The forearm makes a broad diagonal from lower left; the stopped chip group stays at the near edge; the small pot rests beyond the acrylic stop on the right. The rest is textured dark felt and a soft chrome rail. No regulator wheel, bowl, concentric rings or display base.

name: Level 10: Cash King
subject: A seasoned adult cash-game player at the end of a demanding session, calmly organizing multiple chip racks while the last active cash table glows behind. The subject is mastery and endurance across a session, not a crown floating over generic chips.
camera: Cinematic three-quarter rear view at shoulder height, with the player close and the felt visible beyond.
composition: A black jacket and the player's composed profile occupy the left third in silver monochrome. Large orderly chip racks stretch across the lower foreground; the far table fades into ink navy at upper right. A single cobalt desk light creates a human, late-session atmosphere. No crown, circular stage or cards.

name: Hyper Opener
subject: The first betting decision of a three-player spin tournament seen from one seated player's perspective. A black-clothed shoulder and forearm lead into a hand advancing a small opening wager; two opponents across the compact table watch beside balanced early-game chip reserves.
camera: Natural seated eye level just behind the opening player's left shoulder, looking across the felt toward the two opponents. Use a close fifty-millimeter cinematic perspective; no overhead, tilted isometric or bird's-eye view.
composition: The close shoulder frames the left third and the opening hand stretches from lower center toward a small pot at mid-right. Two partial opponent silhouettes occupy the far upper band, with their separate reserves visible. The table is experienced from a chair, not shown as a triangular geometric object. Keep the opening hand and wager large; no display stage, turbine, card reserve area or decorative speed wheel.
revisionReason: Resolve cross-category composition collision identified by root while preserving game-specific focus.

name: Jackpot Pressure
subject: An intimidating high-multiplier prize looms above a tight three-player decision: a huge wall of cobalt prize chips rises behind the small active table, dwarfing the players' immediate betting resources.
camera: Low eye-level view from the table edge, looking upward at the prize scale.
composition: The near table rail and a small live wager form a narrow foreground band. The huge prize-chip wall rises asymmetrically across the upper-right, while three cool monochrome player silhouettes are compressed along the lower-left. Use vertical tension and heavy shadows. No printed multiplier, slot machine, roulette wheel or display platform.

name: Button Limp
subject: A deliberately modest single-chip entry from the button conceals a strong holding and a much deeper reserve in shadow. A plain chrome dealer disc lies beside the entry, while native pocket aces make the trap readable.
camera: Close overhead crop rotated diagonally, with the button corner nearest the viewer.
composition: The small limp chip sits just across the betting line at center. The plain dealer disc is close at lower right; the strong native cards occupy a compact lower-left hand area; the reserve disappears into the upper-right shadow. This is a quiet tactical scene with no trapdoor, mechanical jaws or podium.

name: SNG Endgame
subject: The last two opponents face one another across a compact poker table, while the now-empty third seat is pushed back and falls into darkness. Two unequal remaining stacks and a tight contested pot suggest a decisive heads-up endgame.
camera: Eye-level view from the empty third seat, centered between the final opponents.
composition: The empty seat's dark back partly frames the bottom edge. Two active players in cool monochrome occupy opposite sides, and their hands converge on the small lit felt. The chrome rail forms a shallow horizontal arc. No blades, heroic pedestal or decorative card pair.

name: Phase Shifting
subject: A continuous poker-chip reserve changes from deep to medium to short as it advances along three sharply stepped layers of felt. The available action lanes visibly narrow alongside the shrinking reserves, expressing the changing strategy with stack depth.
camera: Side-on isometric cutaway of a long descending structure.
composition: A tall reserve at upper left leads diagonally down to a compact middle stack and then a short stub at lower right. Three broad layers of black felt and chrome edges overlap; the perspective is architectural and asymmetric. No rotating rings, circular platform or card space.

name: Limb Trap
subject: A small initial limp is followed by an opposing raise, then an exact matching return that keeps the hand alive. Three distinct chip movements trace a broad hooked path across the felt, communicating the limp-call line without any playing cards.
camera: High oblique close-up of the hooked action route, with the caller's side in the near-right foreground.
composition: The early single-chip entry occupies upper left; the opponent's larger raise sweeps through center; the matching return bends toward lower right and remains fully visible. Use physical chip spacing to communicate the sequence, not text, arrows, trap jaws, cards or a display stage.
overlayReview: Native cards omitted to keep the matching return wager fully visible; generated card pixels are removed by a clean-plate correction.

name: 50/50 Survival
subject: A short poker-chip stack pauses just before a risky gap while two equal silver payout ledges remain safely within reach. A few loose chips tumble into the dark gap, emphasizing survival over marginal accumulation.
camera: Steep downward cinematic view over the edge of the gap, with strong foreground depth.
composition: The intact short stack sits large on the near-left felt ledge. Two equally sized illuminated safe ledges occupy the far-right, divided from the player by a sharp dark void. Keep the forms simple, tactile and legible. No balance scale, podium, trophy or playing cards.

name: Aggression Mode
subject: Successive waves of betting chips relentlessly push across a compact table, forcing a smaller opponent reserve toward the rail. The scene shows sustained repeated pressure rather than one isolated all-in.
camera: Fast low tracking angle along the chip movement, with controlled long-exposure traces.
composition: Three broad overlapping chip waves surge from left foreground to right background. The opponent's compact reserve is squeezed into a narrow far-right wedge. Cobalt traces follow the movement over real dark felt; silver edges remain crisp on the nearest wave. No accelerator machine, circular base or cards.

name: Chip Lead Lock
subject: A dominant chip reserve forms a controlled defensive boundary around the player's side of a three-player table, leaving only a narrow deliberate betting lane open. Two smaller opposing reserves remain outside that boundary.
camera: High-angle close crop over the chip leader's side, with the opponents' smaller reserves beyond.
composition: The leader's reserve fills a broad L-shape across the left and bottom edges, occupying most of the frame. A narrow gap opens toward the opponents at upper right, where one measured bet sits. A slim chrome table seam marks control. No literal padlock, tower on a pedestal or decorative cards.

name: Level 10: Spin Master
subject: A complete three-player spin tournament condensed into three bold overlapping snapshots: three active seats and balanced opening reserves, two remaining seats in a close contest, then one collected winning pot. The changing table population tells the full simulation story.
camera: Layered isometric editorial view with each snapshot at a different angle.
composition: Three large slices of black felt overlap down a diagonal from upper left to lower right. The first shows three big seat arcs, the second two, and the final a single dominant winning reserve beside an empty seat. Each slice is broad and simple enough to read on mobile. Use brushed silver and matte cobalt; no spiral trophy, roulette wheel, common display stage or cards.
